newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-News to talk with Packer about League.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-News to talk with Packer about League.

text.p: News Corp Ltd unit News Ltd said on Friday it would talk to Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd about free-to-air television rights for its rebel Super League.
The Federal Court ruled on Friday in favour of an appeal by Rupert Murdoch's media organisation against an earlier court decision barring the rebel league until the end of the century.
News Ltd plans to broadcast its Super League competition in Australia on its 50 percent-owned Foxtel cable television network next year, when the tournament plans to kick off.
"We will have more rugby league now on both free-to-air and pay television through Foxtel," News Ltd managing director Lachlan Murdoch told reporters at a news conference.
"It's open slather to who-ever," Murdoch said. "It will go to the broadcaster who has the most to offer," he said.
Asked if News would sell the free-to-air rights to Packer's Nine Network television station, he replied "If they have the cash to put up...we will listen to them, absolutely."
Packer's Nine Network currently broadcasts the Australian Rugby League (ARL) competition and stands to lose the most from all of Australia's free-to-air broadcasters following today's court ruling.
However, News Ltd chairman Ken Cowley said he would not be rushing into any deal with Packer.
"My memory is they don't seem to like Super League," Cowley told reporters at the news conference.
Packer and Rupert Murdoch's News Corp have been involved in legal brawls with each other this year over other programming deals.
News Corp owns 15 percent of Australian television free-to-air broadcaster Seven Network Ltd, a rival to Packer's Nine Network.
Both Nine and Seven are shareholders in Optus Vision, a rival pay television operator to Foxtel, which News owns in partnership with the Australian government's Telstra telecoms group.
